subject: business-studies
title: HR Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: You'll learn how firms recruit and select staff — internal vs external and key selection tools.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies HR foundations — internal vs external recruitment and selection methods.
final_note: You can describe internal vs external recruitment and the main selection tools used.

concepts.def: Attracting candidates to apply for a job
Choosing the best applicant for the role
Filling a job from existing staff

walkthroughs.body_html:
Internal: cheaper, faster, motivates staff — but limited choice.

External: wider pool and fresh ideas — but slower and costs more in adverts and induction.

Common tools: CV, application form, interview, tests and assessment centres.

Big firms use assessment centres — exercises, presentations, group tasks — to see candidates in action.

A job description lists tasks. A person lists skills/qualities needed.

Together they let candidates self-screen and let HR rank applicants fairly.

mcqs.q: Is external recruitment always better because it brings fresh ideas?
options: Not always — it widens the candidate pool and adds new ideas, but it costs more, takes longer, and the new hire is a bigger unknown than an internal candidate.
Hiring outsiders is automatically superior to promoting existing staff.
Training is only legal for employees under 21.
External recruitment means hiring people from other countries only.

mcqs.q: Is training just an avoidable cost?
options: No — training costs time and money, but it raises productivity, quality and motivation, and can cut staff turnover, so it is also an investment.
Training is only legal for employees under 21.
Cutting training is a cost-free way to save money.
External recruitment means hiring people from other countries only.

mcqs.q: Does money motivate everyone in the same way?
options: No — pay matters, but many workers respond more to praise, responsibility, job variety and career prospects; good managers use financial and non-financial methods together.
Training is only legal for employees under 21.
It is illegal to motivate staff without paying bonuses.
Higher wages are the only effective motivator.
